The overall performance of the EFP Humidifier Filters (wicks) replacement for HDC12 AIRCARE filters (wicks) is affected by one difference. The Aircare HDC12 wick is made with the pass-through of outside air going straight through the wick in see-through channels which picks up the moisture from the wick and carries humid air into my home effectively. The EFP wick has layers that are overlaying one another causing some of the airflow to be restricted resulting for less humidity to be released in the same amount of time.

I found that the water in the Aircare HD1409 humidifier using the HDC12 wick was taking up the water in humidifier containers in about 18 hours requiring them to be refilled. The EFP wick used up about half the water in the same time.

In the dry climate we have in the winter time in Eastern Colorado, we want the humidifier to put out as much moisture as possible. The humidifier has auto sensing to selected humidity and auto-turnoff so getting the right humidity level is not difficult. The EPF wick didn't release enough moisture for the humidifier to turn off once settings were reached. I have family members that live in Oregon that use a similar humidifier but, because the outside humidity is higher, they can use the EPF wick with no problem.

These humidifier filters are definitely low cost.  However the real purpose of these filters is not to filter the air but to wick water from the reservoir to be able to evaporate and add moisture to your house.  For that purpose they work well.

I’ve had these installed for a week or so now. Noticed that the humidifier was going through less water than with very old oem wicks. RH of the garage is also lower. So I touched the wick and it’s mostly dry. Tbf I run these at high speed 24/7 which was never an issue. Idk it’s possible these may work if you’re using this intentionally oversized to keep noise down but these don’t keep up with what the machine is capable of.

I have used these filters over the last 2 winters for my humidifier.  The filters have worked extremely well and have only used 2 sets over 4 months. For those who have had issues with longevity I would suggest the problem is not with the filter but your water that you are using.  Minerals like calcium will build up quickly and harden not allowing the water to be absorbed by the filter.  The harder the water the shorter the life span of the filter.  Using a water treatment in helping prevent calcium and lime buildup will greatly enhance the life of the filters.

I purchased this to get more freezer space as I have a roommate who mostly eats frozen foods and I wanted to be able to stock up on items when there are good sales and also make meals/baked goods in bulk and freeze them to save time and more $. Chest freezers are a challenge to organize but they save SO much energy when compared to upright because every time you open the top, the cold air does not escape. This runs extremely quietly (my wine cooler is much louder). It is pretty large, so do measure your space well and account for the 4 extra inches of space that are recommended on all sides. The black looks much nicer and less of an eyesore than the typical white.

I wish it came with more sliding baskets in the top - it only comes with one. Inside there is one shelf that is actually there to make space for the compressor in the bottom. At first I thought I just needed to settle so I went back and checked it 30 minutes later, it still would not seal. When I lifted the lid I saw that there was black marks on the white insulation. Once I started looking around the outside casing, it appeared that the freezer had been bounced around like a pinball. All the corners were cracked and damaged, the left side had a considerable dent in the top and bottom and the back right corner also had a big dent in it. With all these defects the lid was crooked and for that reason it would not seal. Even with the freezer working properly, without a seal all it is is scrap metal.

In spite of a one year warranty, this freezer (that I previously loved) died in 10 months. As many other reviewers have stated, it's been really impossible to get anyone to honor the warranty.

First, the downloadable warranty offered on this page is for GE Appliances, not Igloo.

On my own, I finally found the Igloo warranty support page and attempted to submit a service ticket, but it kept crashing.

Finally discovered in tiny print that if I was contacting them about an APPLIANCE, I needed to contact an organization called Curtis International.

On the Curtis site, there is no way to submit a service ticket. What there is, however, are instructions for you to ship your appliance back to them PRE-PAID at your OWN expense PLUS include a $7 money order to cover shipping insurance. WTF?! It's a FREEZER that failed to even last one full year and I have to pay to ship it and then some?!?!? So freakin' angry!!!!!

The cost to ship it for warranty coverage is more than the cost of the freezer itself -- and they are counting on you to just write it off.
